title: Global AI Ecosystem Atlas

layers.name: Physical resources
layers.subtitle: Electricity, water, minerals, land and cooling
layers.desc: AI runs on physical machines. Their construction and operation use materials, electricity and cooling; the impact depends on place, time and design.
layers.question: Who supplies the power and water, and who bears the local costs?
layers.evidence: Grid connection agreements, permits, hourly electricity mix, water withdrawals and consumption, equipment supply contracts.

layers.name: Chips
layers.subtitle: Design → fabrication → memory → packaging
layers.desc: Chip designers specify processors. Foundries manufacture silicon; memory and packaging connect the pieces. GPUs accelerate parallel calculations, but CPUs and other accelerators also matter.
layers.question: Which supplier or export restriction could interrupt this system?
layers.evidence: Supplier filings, chip specifications, fabrication and packaging locations, export licences.

layers.name: Compute
layers.subtitle: Data centres, cloud services and public supercomputers
layers.desc: Compute is the capacity to run calculations. A cloud sells access to machines; a data centre houses them. Public research clusters serve different users from commercial clouds.
layers.question: Who can access capacity, at what price, and under whose jurisdiction?
layers.evidence: Live service-region lists, access rules, procurement records, utilisation and queue times.

layers.name: Data & human labour
layers.subtitle: Collection, licensing, annotation and evaluation
layers.desc: People collect, clean, label and evaluate data. Training material can include licensed, public, personal and synthetic data. Publicly accessible does not automatically mean freely reusable.
layers.question: Whose work and language are represented, paid for or excluded?
layers.evidence: Dataset documentation, licences, worker contracts, pay records, consent and grievance procedures.

layers.name: Models
layers.subtitle: Learned parameters for language, images, speech and prediction
layers.desc: Training changes numerical parameters using examples and an objective. Inference applies a trained model to new inputs. An LLM generates tokens from context; fluent output can still be wrong.
layers.question: What was trained, on which data, and how was performance independently tested?
layers.evidence: Model cards, training reports, evaluation datasets, licences and reproducible tests.

layers.name: Developer tools
layers.subtitle: Frameworks, APIs, model hubs and retrieval
layers.desc: Tools help developers train, access and connect models. An API is a service interface. Retrieval adds documents at use time; agents can call tools and carry out actions.
layers.question: Which external services receive user data or control essential functions?
layers.evidence: Architecture diagrams, API terms, data-flow logs, retention rules and tool permissions.

layers.name: Applications
layers.subtitle: Chat, translation, speech, recommendations and decisions
layers.desc: Applications combine models with interfaces, business rules and people. AI also ranks content, predicts demand and detects patterns; it extends far beyond chatbots.
layers.question: What changes for the person affected, and can they challenge the outcome?
layers.evidence: Before/after workflow records, error rates by group, appeals, incidents and user interviews.

layers.name: Research & communities
layers.subtitle: Cross-cutting: knowledge, skills, evaluation and alternatives
layers.desc: Universities, public labs and communities create methods, datasets and skills across every layer. Commercial research and public research overlap, but incentives and access differ.
layers.question: Who funds the research, sets the benchmark and gets to reproduce it?
layers.evidence: Funding disclosures, publications, compute access and participation rules.

layers.name: Governance & accountability
layers.subtitle: Cross-cutting: laws, standards, oversight and civil society
layers.desc: Governance shapes the entire lifecycle. Binding laws, voluntary frameworks, ethical recommendations and watchdog reporting are different instruments.
layers.question: Who has enforceable authority, and what remedy exists when AI causes harm?
layers.evidence: Legal texts, regulator decisions, audits, procurement rules and complaint records.

organizations.name: Schneider Electric
organizations.description: Supplies power management and cooling systems for data centres.
organizations.operations: Global equipment provider; a location marker does not identify a particular customer.
organizations.prompt: Does the efficiency claim include the whole facility and its energy source?

organizations.name: ASML
organizations.description: Makes lithography equipment used to manufacture chips.
organizations.operations: R&D/manufacturing in the Netherlands, US, Germany and Asia; selected sites shown in operations view.
organizations.prompt: Where do components come from, and which sales require licences?

organizations.name: Tokyo Electron
organizations.description: Supplies semiconductor production equipment.
organizations.operations: Equipment and service business across chipmaking markets.
organizations.prompt: Which processing steps depend on imported equipment?

organizations.name: NVIDIA
organizations.description: Designs GPUs and supplies the CUDA software platform.
organizations.operations: Chip manufacturing is performed by partners; selected TSMC production is documented separately.
organizations.prompt: Does software lock-in matter as much as the price of hardware?

organizations.name: TSMC
organizations.description: Contract foundry manufacturing chips for other companies.
organizations.operations: Headquarters in Taiwan; selected Arizona manufacturing shown separately.
organizations.prompt: Where are fabrication and packaging actually performed?

organizations.name: SK hynix
organizations.description: Makes memory, including high-bandwidth memory used in AI computing.
organizations.operations: Icheon and Cheongju fabrication; overseas sites are not exhaustively mapped.
organizations.prompt: Could a memory or packaging bottleneck constrain deployment?

organizations.name: Arm
organizations.description: Provides processor architecture and design technology.
organizations.operations: Global offices and technology licensing; manufacturing is a separate activity.
organizations.prompt: Who owns the design rights and controls the licence?

organizations.name: Amazon Web Services
organizations.description: Cloud infrastructure and managed AI services.
organizations.operations: Global cloud regions; consult the live region list for any specific workload.
organizations.prompt: Which region runs the workload and who controls encryption keys?

organizations.name: OVHcloud
organizations.description: Cloud infrastructure with GPU services for AI.
organizations.operations: International data centres; headquarters and compute location are distinct.
organizations.prompt: Can the customer move its models and data to another provider?

organizations.name: Alibaba Cloud
organizations.description: Cloud infrastructure with locations across multiple markets.
organizations.operations: Operating cloud regions are listed separately from announced regions.
organizations.prompt: Which service region and legal entity actually handle the data?

organizations.name: Appen
organizations.description: Provides human-supported AI data collection, annotation and evaluation.
organizations.operations: Corporate HQ Sydney; US HQ Kirkland; offices listed in the UK, China, Japan, the Philippines, India and Vietnam.
organizations.prompt: How are task rates, rejected work and worker appeals handled?

organizations.name: Sama
organizations.description: Provides human-verified data annotation and evaluation.
organizations.operations: Documented teams in Kenya and Uganda. In 2026 Meta ended an annotation contract after reporting on smart-glasses footage, and Sama issued 1,108 redundancy notices. Earlier, Sama workers labelled harmful text for OpenAI.
organizations.prompt: Can workers verify pay, monitoring and grievance claims?

organizations.name: Common Crawl
organizations.description: Makes web crawl datasets available for research and other uses.
organizations.operations: The corpus is global; a US organizational base does not describe the origins of all data.
organizations.prompt: Which sites, languages and rights are included or excluded?

organizations.name: Masakhane
organizations.description: Grassroots research community for African-language NLP.
organizations.operations: Distributed participants; no single headquarters is assigned.
organizations.prompt: Who decides language priorities, and who owns the resulting resources?

organizations.name: OpenAI
organizations.description: Develops AI models, APIs and ChatGPT.
organizations.operations: Products and research reach many markets; a base marker does not locate every inference request.
organizations.prompt: Which model/version, data practices and evaluations support the claim?

organizations.name: Anthropic
organizations.description: Develops Claude models, products and safety research.
organizations.operations: Multi-cloud: AWS is its primary training and cloud provider; it also announced up to one million Google TPUs (October 2025) and a $30 billion Azure commitment on NVIDIA systems (November 2025).
organizations.prompt: How much control rests with cloud partners and model operators?

organizations.name: Google DeepMind
organizations.description: AI research organization developing models and scientific applications.
organizations.operations: Part of Google; research teams and deployment infrastructure span countries.
organizations.prompt: Who can independently reproduce a scientific or benchmark claim?

organizations.name: Mistral AI
organizations.description: Develops AI models and services, including Le Chat.
organizations.operations: Model access and licence terms vary by release; check the specific model card.
organizations.prompt: Is this an open-weight release, an API service or both?

organizations.name: DeepSeek
organizations.description: Develops language models, chat and API services.
organizations.operations: Service operator is Hangzhou DeepSeek; downloaded weights and hosted services have different data flows.
organizations.prompt: Is the story about model weights or the hosted application?

organizations.name: Sarvam AI
organizations.description: Develops text, speech and language AI for Indian languages.
organizations.operations: Bengaluru address; multilingual models and APIs serve Indian-language use cases.
organizations.prompt: What do independent tests show for dialects and code-switching?

organizations.name: AI Singapore / SEA-LION
organizations.description: Develops multilingual models and evaluation resources for Southeast Asia.
organizations.operations: Regional language coverage; the program is based in Singapore.
organizations.prompt: Which languages and cultural contexts are tested by local speakers?

organizations.name: Technology Innovation Institute
organizations.description: Applied research institute associated with the Falcon model family.
organizations.operations: UAE research base; availability and licences depend on the model release.
organizations.prompt: What can outside researchers inspect and reproduce?

organizations.name: CENIA / LatamGPT
organizations.description: AI research centre coordinating a Latin American language-model initiative.
organizations.operations: Latam-GPT launched in February 2026: a 70-billion-parameter model adapted from Meta’s Llama 3.1 and reportedly trained on AWS. Chilean coordination is not the location of every contributor.
organizations.prompt: Who contributed the corpus, and how are regional communities represented?

organizations.name: Lelapa AI
organizations.description: Builds multilingual speech and translation tools, including Vulavula.
organizations.operations: Focus on African-language and code-switching use cases; no city-level HQ claim here.
organizations.prompt: Can performance be verified on real local-language calls?

organizations.name: Hugging Face
organizations.description: Hosts models, datasets and developer collaboration tools.
organizations.operations: International platform and community; hosted repositories have their own licences.
organizations.prompt: Does a repository licence cover its data as well as its weights?

organizations.name: PyTorch Foundation
organizations.description: Supports the PyTorch machine-learning software ecosystem.
organizations.operations: Under the Linux Foundation; development is distributed internationally.
organizations.prompt: Who funds maintenance and can users reproduce or audit the code?

organizations.name: DeepL
organizations.description: Provides translation, writing and language-service interfaces.
organizations.operations: Cologne registered office; users and product availability span markets.
organizations.prompt: Which text is retained, and where do translation errors affect meaning?

organizations.name: Mila
organizations.description: Nonprofit AI research institute bringing together university researchers.
organizations.operations: Montréal research base; international collaborations.
organizations.prompt: How do sponsor funding and compute access shape research priorities?

organizations.name: RIKEN R-CCS
organizations.description: Research centre for computational science and supercomputing.
organizations.operations: Kobe centre; public scientific computing serves multiple fields, including AI research.
organizations.prompt: Who receives allocations and what research can the public inspect?

organizations.name: LNCC / Santos Dumont
organizations.description: National scientific computing laboratory hosting Santos Dumont.
organizations.operations: Brazilian research computing infrastructure; not exclusively an AI facility.
organizations.prompt: How much public compute is available to researchers beyond major cities?

organizations.name: Data Science Nigeria
organizations.description: Builds AI skills, research and social-impact applications.
organizations.operations: Lagos research centre and broader training activity; international collaborations.
organizations.prompt: Who gains skills and access, and what benefits are measured?

organizations.name: CSIRO
organizations.description: Australia’s national science agency conducts AI research and applied work.
organizations.operations: Multiple Australian sites; marker represents the agency rather than a particular lab.
organizations.prompt: What problem, validation and public benefit justify the project?

organizations.name: UNESCO
organizations.description: Publishes a global recommendation on AI ethics.
organizations.operations: International membership; an ethical recommendation is distinct from domestic enforcement.
organizations.prompt: Who translates the principles into funded and enforceable practice?

organizations.name: OECD.AI
organizations.description: Provides AI policy analysis, principles and incident resources.
organizations.operations: Intergovernmental work; member coverage is not universal global representation.
organizations.prompt: Whose incidents and national experiences are visible in the data?

organizations.name: European Commission / AI Office
organizations.description: EU institutions implement and coordinate the AI Act framework.
organizations.operations: The AI Act applies in phases: general-purpose AI model rules since August 2025 and transparency duties since August 2026. The 2026 Digital Omnibus moved high-risk rules to 2 December 2027 (stand-alone) and 2 August 2028 (in regulated products).
organizations.prompt: Which obligation applies, who supervises it, and what evidence exists?

organizations.name: NIST
organizations.description: Publishes the voluntary AI Risk Management Framework.
organizations.operations: US standards institute; voluntary use is distinct from a binding legal requirement.
organizations.prompt: Is the company reporting actual controls or only claiming alignment?

organizations.name: AlgorithmWatch
organizations.description: Investigates automated systems and their effects on society.
organizations.operations: European civil-society work; it is not a regulator.
organizations.prompt: Who can investigate systems that companies keep opaque?

organizations.name: TÜBİTAK ULAKBİM / TRUBA
organizations.description: Provides national research computing, including ARF and the ARF-ACC GPU cluster.
organizations.operations: Published ARF-ACC queue documentation lists NVIDIA H100/H200 hardware.
organizations.prompt: Who gets GPU time, how long are queues, and which suppliers support the cluster?

organizations.name: Turkcell
organizations.description: Operates domestic data-centre/cloud infrastructure and has a planned Google Cloud region partnership.
organizations.operations: Existing infrastructure differs from the planned Google region, which Turkcell estimates will operate in 2028-2029; Turkcell plans to invest $1 billion in data centres and cloud.
organizations.prompt: Which capacity is live, and which part is an investment commitment?

organizations.name: T3 Foundation / T3 AI
organizations.description: Turkish-language model and community initiative led by T3 Foundation and developed with Baykar.
organizations.operations: The foundation describes an open-source project; inspect release artefacts before treating that as a licence classification.
organizations.prompt: What data, weights, code and evaluation are actually available?

organizations.name: HAVELSAN / MAIN
organizations.description: Provides the MAIN enterprise AI platform, including deployment on closed networks.
organizations.operations: Company markets domestic AI capabilities; the claim does not establish a wholly domestic supply chain.
organizations.prompt: Which components are developed locally, licensed or imported?

organizations.name: SESTEK
organizations.description: Develops conversational automation and speech technology.
organizations.operations: Turkish operating base; part of Unifonic, illustrating ownership beyond the local ecosystem.
organizations.prompt: Where are models, customer recordings and ownership decisions located?

organizations.name: Boğaziçi University / BOUN Treebank
organizations.description: University research includes manually annotated Turkish-language resources.
organizations.operations: BOUN Treebank is a documented research resource; the cited paper is historical, not a 2026 release claim.
organizations.prompt: Who annotates Turkish data, and what licence and coverage limits apply?

organizations.name: Türkiye AI Initiative (TRAI)
organizations.description: Connects businesses, provides training and maintains an AI startup map.
organizations.operations: A commercial ecosystem platform, not an independent regulator; its directory is a discovery tool.
organizations.prompt: Does being listed establish deployment, revenue or original model development?

organizations.name: KVKK
organizations.description: Türkiye’s personal-data protection authority publishes guidance on generative AI.
organizations.operations: Personal-data oversight; guidance must be distinguished from statutory obligations and decisions.
organizations.prompt: Where is personal data sent, and what lawful basis and remedy exist?

organizations.name: Ministry of Industry and Technology
organizations.description: Coordinates industrial technology policy and the Türkiye AI Action Plan (2026-2030).
organizations.operations: The plan entered into force through Presidential Circular 2026/9 (Official Gazette, 18 August 2026). Targets are commitments, not evidence of delivery.
organizations.prompt: Which budgets, responsible agencies, milestones and progress reports back the plan’s targets?

organizations.name: Statkraft
organizations.description: Offers renewable electricity and site solutions for data centres.
organizations.operations: Norwegian site offerings and power-market activities; no named customer dependency is inferred.
organizations.prompt: Does the renewable claim describe annual certificates or hourly power matching?

organizations.name: Glencore
organizations.description: Produces and markets metals including copper and cobalt.
organizations.operations: Global mining and commodity activities; inclusion illustrates material foundations, not supply to a named AI vendor.
organizations.prompt: Can a particular material be traced from a mine to this infrastructure?

organizations.name: Google / Google Cloud
organizations.description: Designs TPU accelerators, sells cloud capacity and develops Gemini models; parent of Google DeepMind.
organizations.operations: Cloud regions worldwide, including a planned Türkiye region with Turkcell. TPUs are Google-designed chips made by partner foundries.
organizations.prompt: Which workloads run on Google’s own chips, and which on rented NVIDIA hardware?

organizations.name: Meta
organizations.description: Publishes Llama open-weight models and runs social platforms and AI-enabled devices.
organizations.operations: Llama weights come with Meta’s own licence terms, which models built on them inherit. Human review of device data has involved outsourced annotators.
organizations.prompt: Which licence terms and data practices travel with a model built on Llama?

organizations.name: Huawei (Ascend)
organizations.description: Designs Ascend AI processors and sells AI computing systems and cloud services.
organizations.operations: On the US Entity List since 2019; 2025 US guidance warns that using certain Ascend chips anywhere may breach US export controls. Illustrates a parallel chip ecosystem.
organizations.prompt: Which export rules, suppliers and software stack does a non-NVIDIA alternative depend on?

organizations.name: TÜBİTAK BİLGEM / BİLGE
organizations.description: TÜBİTAK’s informatics institute develops BİLGE, a Turkish large-language-model family unveiled in June 2026.
organizations.operations: TÜBİTAK said in June 2026 that BİLGE was not yet a public service. Parameter counts and benchmark claims in media reports differ and are not independently verified.
organizations.prompt: Which BİLGE models, training data, evaluations and access terms are actually published?

dependencies.label: NVIDIA → TSMC: chip fabrication
dependencies.desc: On 17 October 2025 NVIDIA announced the first Blackwell wafer produced at TSMC Arizona. Advanced CoWoS packaging still took place in Taiwan, so this is neither an end-to-end US-made chip nor evidence that every NVIDIA chip is made there.

dependencies.label: Anthropic → AWS: training/cloud capacity
dependencies.desc: In April 2026 Anthropic again named AWS its primary training and cloud provider, with up to 5 GW of new capacity planned. Future capacity is not all live, and Anthropic also uses Google TPUs and NVIDIA systems on Azure.

dependencies.label: TRUBA ARF-ACC → NVIDIA: GPU hardware
dependencies.desc: The published queue table identifies NVIDIA H100 and H200 GPUs. This does not establish a direct procurement contract with NVIDIA. Under the US AI Diffusion Rule of January 2025, Türkiye faced capped access to such chips; the rule was rescinded in May 2025 before taking effect.

dependencies.label: Turkcell ↔ Google Cloud: planned Türkiye region
dependencies.desc: Google announced a Türkiye cloud region with Turkcell in November 2025, citing a 10-year, $2 billion investment; Turkcell estimates operation in 2028-2029. Existing Turkcell data centres are not relabelled as that region.

dependencies.label: Anthropic → Google Cloud: TPU capacity
dependencies.desc: Anthropic announced in October 2025 that it would use up to one million Google Cloud TPUs, with well over a gigawatt expected online in 2026. Announced capacity is not all live.

dependencies.label: Anthropic → Microsoft Azure / NVIDIA: compute commitment
dependencies.desc: In November 2025 Anthropic committed to buy $30 billion of Azure compute, initially up to one gigawatt on NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems. A purchase commitment is not capacity in use.

dependencies.label: Meta → Sama: data annotation (ended 2026)
dependencies.desc: Sama annotators in Kenya labelled footage from Meta’s smart glasses. After Swedish reporting in February 2026 on intimate footage, Meta ended the contract and Sama issued 1,108 redundancy notices. Meta says Sama did not meet its standards; Sama disputes this.

dependencies.label: Latam-GPT → Meta Llama: base model
dependencies.desc: Latam-GPT, launched in February 2026, adapts Meta’s Llama-3.1-70B and is distributed under the Llama 3.1 licence. A regional model can still depend on a foreign base model’s weights and terms.

glossary: AI / machine learning
AI is a broad field. Machine learning fits models from data; it includes prediction, ranking and generation.
Neural network
A model with connected numerical parameters that are adjusted during training.
Transformer
A neural-network architecture using attention to relate parts of an input; influential in language and multimodal models.
Training / inference
Training changes model parameters. Inference uses a trained model to calculate an output. An ordinary prompt does not necessarily retrain the model.
Token / context
Tokens are chunks of input/output. Context is the information available for the current calculation; it is not the entire training dataset.
Parameters / weights
The numerical values learned during training. Model size alone does not establish quality or truth.
Fine-tuning / retrieval
Fine-tuning adjusts weights. Retrieval fetches material into the current context, typically without changing weights.
Open weights / open source
Downloadable weights do not by themselves establish open-source status. Check code, data information, licences and permitted uses for the exact release.
API / agent
An API exposes a service to software. An agent combines models with tools and a workflow to take actions.
Hallucination / evaluation
A plausible but unsupported output is often called a hallucination. Evaluate task performance and errors by language, group and context.
Data sovereignty
Ask separately about location, legal control, ownership, infrastructure suppliers, access and practical exit options.
methodology: Editorial sample, not a ranking or census. Selected to show distinct functions, institution types, regions and language communities. One organization may occupy several layers. Blank areas mean omitted examples, not absence of AI activity. HQ/base markers describe organizations, not all compute, workers, users or ownership. Coordinates are approximate city or country positions, not facility addresses. Operations are a deliberately small sourced sample. No marker size encodes market share. Sources checked on 8 October 2026, with corrections and additions checked on 9 October 2026; historical reports retain their dates. Company statements verify stated products/relationships, not claimed accuracy or social benefit. Some official pages were accessible only as indexed excerpts; these are labelled in the source register.
turkiye: TRUBA research computing; domestic commercial data centres; Turkish-language models such as T3 AI, BİLGE and MAIN; speech and enterprise applications.
ARF-ACC uses NVIDIA hardware. Turkcell’s Google region is planned. SESTEK has an Istanbul base and Unifonic ownership. Each demonstrates a different kind of international connection.

The Türkiye AI Action Plan (2026-2030) entered into force through Presidential Circular 2026/9 on 18 August 2026. Its targets include at least 1 GW of data-centre capacity by 2030. Obtain budgets, responsible agencies and progress reports before judging delivery; the 2021-2025 strategy is now historical context.

Separate training origin, model licence, Turkish evaluation, data location, legal control, chip/cloud suppliers and procurement. A Turkish interface or local deployment proves none of the other dimensions.
